en: Itivuttaka 6: Ekakanipāta, Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter) Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard. "Monks, there is one thing that, when developed and cultivated, leads to the abandoning of all unwholesome states. What is that one thing? Mindfulness directed to the body (*kāyagatāsati*). This, monks, is that one thing which, when developed and cultivated, leads to the abandoning of all unwholesome states. Thus it was said by the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: "Friend Ānanda, what is the name of this discourse spoken by the Blessed One? "It is called *Kāyagatāsati*, friend," he replied. "But, friend, how does this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* lead to the abandoning of all unwholesome states? "Come, friend, let us approach the Blessed One. Having approached, we shall ask the Blessed One about the meaning of this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we shall bear it in mind. "Yes, friend," that monk replied to the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Venerable Ānanda and that monk approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "Just now, Lord, a certain monk approached me and asked me: 'Friend Ānanda, what is the name of this discourse spoken by the Blessed One? I replied: 'It is called *Kāyagatāsati*, friend. Then he asked: 'But, friend, how does this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* lead to the abandoning of all unwholesome states? I said to him: 'Come, friend, let us approach the Blessed One... so we shall bear it in mind. "Ānanda, I have taught you this very discourse on *Kāyagatāsati*. How, Ānanda, does this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* lead to the abandoning of all unwholesome states? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut, sits down; having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him, ever mindful he breathes in, mindful he breathes out. Breathing in long, he knows: 'I breathe in long'; or breathing out long, he knows: 'I breathe out long. Breathing in short, he knows: 'I breathe in short'; or breathing out short, he knows: 'I breathe out short. He trains thus: 'Experiencing the whole body, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Experiencing the whole body, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Tranquillizing the bodily formation, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Tranquillizing the bodily formation, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Experiencing rapture, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Experiencing rapture, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Experiencing the mental formation, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Experiencing the mental formation, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Tranquillizing the mental formation, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Tranquillizing the mental formation, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Experiencing the mind, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Experiencing the mind, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Gladdening the mind, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Gladdening the mind, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Concentrating the mind, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Concentrating the mind, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Liberating the mind, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Liberating the mind, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Contemplating impermanence, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Contemplating impermanence, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Contemplating fading away, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Contemplating fading away, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Contemplating cessation, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Contemplating cessation, I shall breathe out. He trains thus: 'Contemplating relinquishment, I shall breathe in'; he trains thus: 'Contemplating relinquishment, I shall breathe out. In this way, Ānanda, this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* leads to the abandoning of all unwholesome states. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, soon after the Blessed One had departed, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus! "Yes, friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda said this: "Friends, this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* was taught by the Blessed One in brief, with its meaning fully explained, and with its details fully analyzed. As for me, friends, I remember this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* exactly as it was spoken by the Blessed One. If it seems appropriate to you, friends, let us go to the Blessed One and report this matter to him. As the Blessed One explains it to us, so we shall bear it in mind. "Yes, friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Venerable Ānanda and those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation that had taken place between himself and those bhikkhus. "Good, good, Ānanda! It is well that you remember this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* exactly as it was spoken by me. Indeed, Ānanda, this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* was taught by me in brief, with its meaning fully explained, and with its details fully analyzed. Therefore, Ānanda, remember this discourse on *Kāyagatāsati* exactly as it was spoken by me. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Delighted, the Venerable Ānanda and those bhikkhus rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. [End of] Itivuttaka 6: Ekakanipāta, Paṭhamavagga. The First Chapter. The Section on the Single Discourses. The Sixth Sutta. The Discourse on the One Thing. Thus it was said. The First Chapter is finished. The *Ekakanipāta* is finished. The *Itivuttaka* is finished. The *Khuddakapāṭha* is finished. The *Suttasaṅgaha* is finished. The *Khuddakanikāya* is finished. The Tipiṭaka is finished. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. May there be well-being. This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
I am your guarantor for non-returning.
Monks, abandon the one thing, which is conceit.
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
“Having fully understood that conceit by which beings, intoxicated with pride, go to an evil destination— ”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
